刮葫屬於裂縫鼓一類，發聲來自空心原木外殼上的裂縫。以一對木槌敲擊裂縫時，封閉兩端: The huiringua belongs to the class of slit drums, and its sound comes from a slit in the shell of a hollow log. When the slit is struck with a pair of wooden mallets the wooden shell, closed at both ends, becomes the resonator and produces the struck sound of an idiophone. The source gives no range and no means of controlling volume, and does not say how it differs concretely from other instruments of the family.
刮葫的琴身由一段兩端封閉的空心原木構成，沿器身開有一道縫隙，外殼同時作為共鳴腔。: The body of the huiringua is a length of hollow log closed at both ends with a slit cut along it, and the shell serves as the resonator. The sounding part is that slit, struck with a wooden mallet. The source states only that the body is hollow log and the beater a wooden mallet; it says nothing about other parts or the kind of wood.
刮葫（Huiringua）是墨西哥的體鳴打擊樂器，屬於裂縫鼓一類，Hornbos: The huiringua is a Mexican struck idiophone of the slit-drum class, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.243. It is built from a length of hollow log closed at both ends, with a slit cut along the body; the shell itself becomes the resonator. It is played by striking the slit with a pair of wooden mallets so that the wood vibrates and sounds. The source does not say on what occasions or by whom it is played, so no guess is made here.

演奏刮葫時，以一對木槌敲擊沿空心原木的裂縫，使封閉兩端的原木外殼成為共鳴腔而發聲: The huiringua is played by striking the slit along the hollow log with a pair of wooden mallets, so that the log shell closed at both ends becomes the resonator and sounds. A beginner can first practise striking the slit steadily, so that every stroke meets the same spot and produces a clear resonance. The source gives no playing posture, no way of holding the mallets and no teaching steps, so only the basic order of actions can be described here, following how the instrument sounds.
